about: The Store 014 ontology for Season 2: the things the store sells, moves and gets paid for, the links between them, twelve rules and what each record sees. Every rule is a Season 1 fix written down; 'solves' names the Season 1 KPIs (ids from domain-kpis.yaml).

things.name: Product
things.says: what a customer asks for: whole-wheat atta

things.name: Item
things.says: the pack: a 5 kg bag, known by the GTIN on it

things.name: Place
things.says: a warehouse slot, the store's shelf or backroom

things.name: Customer
things.says: wants items, pays bills, has a bank account

things.name: Store order
things.says: cases of an item, for Store 014

things.name: Pick
things.says: cases taken from a warehouse slot

things.name: Case
things.says: packs of exactly one item

things.name: Pallet
things.says: cases, known by the SSCC label

things.name: Shipment
things.says: pallets on a truck, in a delivery window

things.name: Receiving
things.says: the store takes in the pallets

things.name: Stock
things.says: packs of an item at a place, now

things.name: Stock change
things.says: receipt, sale, write-off or count, with a reason

things.name: Forecast
things.says: expected demand, per day

things.name: Demand
things.says: a customer wants an item

things.name: Sale
things.says: demand met from the shelf

things.name: Lost sale
things.says: demand that found the shelf empty

things.name: Bill
things.says: one checkout: its lines and total

things.name: Payment attempt
things.says: a UPI request for a bill, with its RRN

things.name: Debit
things.says: money taken from the customer's bank

things.name: Settlement
things.says: the store's bank credited, daily

things.name: Refund
things.says: an extra debit given back

things.name: Complaint
things.says: a customer reports a debit

rules.text: Available means on the shelf. Book stock is a belief – the last count, plus receipts, minus sales and write-offs.
Silence is a question. No sales while the books show stock means someone should look at the shelf.
Demand is not sales. Demand that finds an empty shelf becomes a lost sale, which no record holds – estimate it and say how.
A forecast predicts demand, so score it against demand, not sales.
Every stock correction has a reason. Mirror-image corrections on lookalike items, neighboring slots or two buildings are one event.
Fresh stock expires. Waste and the empty shelf are one decision – count both.
An item is the pack, known by the code on the pack. Match on that code – never on the slot, the pallet label or the product name.
A delivery is on time, in full and right – checked case by case at the door, and done only when the stock is on the shelf.
A payment has three witnesses – the till, UPI and the banks. A timeout at the till means “not known yet”, and UPI's final status decides.
One bill, one payment. Every UPI request carries the bill ID, and a debit with no approved payment is a customer charged twice until proven otherwise.
A refund answers a debit. The clock starts at the extra debit, not at the complaint.
Every record either looks at the world or copies another record. Before acting on a KPI, find the record it reads and an observation that can contradict it.
